text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Monday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Riga municipal election committee started to register lists of candidates for the coming municipal elections on March 9. The Latvia's Farmers Union was the first to register with 20 other parties preparing lists.
- The Fatherland & Freedom party has presented its municipal election list, headed by secretary general Maris Argalis, director of a Riga district board.
- The Latvian Conservative Union and the Union of Reforms, both founded last year, have formed an election alliance, supporting the idea of young, well-educated people entering politics.

- Joachim Siegerist, co-chairman of the populist People's Movement For Latvia, advertises in the northern German paper Lingener Tagespost calling on Germans to participate in his charity campaign donating to Latvians in need.
- The former finance minister, Aivars Kreituss, expresses concerns that the Democratic Party Saimnieks may use the post of Finance Minister for selfish purposes.
- A contraband cargo worth about 100,000 lats was arrested on January 17 by police in the Saldus district. The cargo is reported to contain a large quantity of jewellery.
- Russia's new ambassador to Latvia, Alexander Udaltsov, is due to arrive in Riga tomorrow and will present his credentials to President Guntis Ulmanis on January 28.
- President Guntis Ulmanis believes seeing the occupation museum in Riga should be included into the protocol programme for visiting foreign ambassadors.

- The board of the Latvian Shipping Company has elaborated a plan to dramatically restructure its economic and financial activities. Streamlining the company's governing bodies and reducing the number of ships carrying the Latvian flag are among the measures to cut losses.
- The prime minister will suggest passing a two-year budget for 1998-99 to create a stable business environment.
